page.layout: Running head at top centre, page number at top left; below them two round woodcut medallions side by side (the legends printed on them are transcribed first); one block of running text, full width, with two paragraphs; below the text a decorative woodcut ornament, not text, so not transcribed.

main_text.l: PERSEVS Iouis filius ex Danaë, Medusam Gorgonem
occidit, anno mundi 2497. ante Christum natum 1465. Hic
à Græcia in Asiam transfuectus est: ibi Barbaras gentes graui,
diuturnóque bello domuit: & nouissimè victor, nomen supe-
ratæ genti dedit:nanque à Perseo Persæ dicti sunt. Vide Orof.
lib.1.cap.11. De hoc quoq; sic inquit Herodotus lib.7. Posteaquā

l.i: Perseus ad Cepheum cōmeauit, & Andromedam eius filiam duxit vxo-
rem,tulit ex ea filium,quem Persen appellauit:eúmque illic reliquit (nam

main_text.l: Cepheus carebat virili prole) à quo cognomen sortiti sunt Persæ. De Per-
seo,Poëtæ multi multa fabulantur. Vide Diodo.lib.1.& 4.
pes filia, vxor fuit Persei, quam scopulo alligatam ac monstro
marino, propter matris superbiam, vt aiunt, expositam, libera-
uit: liberatam in vxorē duxit, occisis Phineo, & reliquis aduer-
santibus. Acrisiū qui Danaën turri incluserat, occidit Perseus,
imprudens tamen. Vide Herodo.lib.7. & Diodorum Siculum

page.notes: The two medallions are woodcut portraits. The legend on the left reads PERSEVS and ARGIVI REX; the legend on the right reads ANDROMEDA and PERS, the last word partly cut off by the medallion edge. The bottom ornament is a decorative woodcut without text. The scan is slightly blurred in the italic line, but the words are legible.
